output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August move of the alert relay server, not by agency nurses. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A-C then went from about 38 to about 82 phone alerts per nurse per shift, and acknowledgement time doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, did not change. Incidents rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses in the affected pods, and monitor alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the September monitor update don't explain it. The risk is alarm fatigue, which probably also contributes to the higher sick leave, though that link is unproven. I'd reject the agency cap and the performance reviews, because they would punish the wrong people. I'd also reject stopping phone forwarding of SpO2 alarms. Restore the old rules with Clinical Engineering validation and committee sign-off, then track alerts per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Confidence is high. Wireless coverage was not directly tested, but the pattern doesn't point to it.
